controls.name: begin-refused
controls.replace: Msg::Begin => (S { store: s.store, failed: true, tx: None }, Ans::Failure),
controls.classification: repair (alternative): BEGIN refused with FAILURE, as design Refuse; the client is told there is no transaction, so every as-built departure theorem and the commit neighbor change

controls.name: atomic-tx
controls.classification: repair (intended): BEGIN opens a transaction whose writes are held until COMMIT; ROLLBACK, RESET and a closed connection discard them

controls.name: rollback-answers-failure
controls.classification: answer: ROLLBACK answered FAILURE instead of SUCCESS (the client would learn the writes stayed)

controls.name: run-not-committed
controls.classification: decision: a successful RUN's write not committed by execute_cypher (removes P-AUTOCOMMIT); the auto-commit neighbor and every theorem built on the lemma lose their store

controls.name: failed-run-writes
controls.classification: premise P-STMT-ATOMIC flipped: a failing statement keeps its own writes

controls.name: failure-not-sticky
controls.classification: decision: the FAILED state's guard removed, so PULL and ROLLBACK after a failure are no longer IGNORED

controls.name: rule-rollback-keeps
controls.find: Msg::Rollback => C { store: c.store, tx: None, failed: false },
controls.replace: Msg::Rollback => match c.tx { Some(p) => C { store: c.store + p, tx: None, failed: false }, None => c },
controls.classification: rule weakened: the client ledger keeps a rolled-back transaction's writes (checks that the departure theorems constrain the rule, not only the server)

controls.name: http-batch-atomic
controls.find: HOut { store: r.0, ran: r.1, errors: r.2, status: if r.2 == 0 { HStatus::Ok200 } else { HStatus::Bad400 } }
controls.replace: HOut { store: if r.2 == 0 { r.0 } else { store }, ran: r.1, errors: r.2, status: if r.2 == 0 { HStatus::Ok200 } else { HStatus::Bad400 } }
controls.classification: repair (intended, G1): a request with a failed statement is rolled back whole, so no statement's writes stay; every as-built departure theorem must change

controls.name: http-stop-at-failure
controls.find:
let r = run_all(if st.fails { store } else { store + st.w }, b.drop_first());
        (r.0, r.1 + 1, r.2 + (if st.fails { 1nat } else { 0nat }))
controls.replace:
let r = run_all(if st.fails { store } else { store + st.w }, b.drop_first());
        if st.fails { (store, 1, 1) } else { (r.0, r.1 + 1, r.2) }
controls.classification: decision 390-399: the loop stops at the first failing statement (Neo4j's order) instead of continuing; the statements after the failure no longer run, so ran and the kept writes change

controls.name: http-failure-writes
controls.find: let r = run_all(if st.fails { store } else { store + st.w }, b.drop_first());
controls.classification: premise P-STMT-ATOMIC flipped: a failing statement keeps its own writes

controls.name: http-read-only-runs-reads
controls.find: if read_only && any_named(b) { HOut { store: store, ran: 0, errors: 1, status: HStatus::Forbidden403 } }
controls.replace: if read_only && any_named(b) { HOut { store: store, ran: b.len(), errors: 1, status: HStatus::Forbidden403 } }
controls.classification: decision 379-384: the read-only gate refuses only the writing statements and still runs the reads (ADMIN_API: none of its statements run)

controls.name: http-status-ok-on-error
controls.find: HOut { store: r.0, ran: r.1, errors: r.2, status: if r.2 == 0 { HStatus::Ok200 } else { HStatus::Bad400 } }
controls.replace: HOut { store: r.0, ran: r.1, errors: r.2, status: HStatus::Ok200 }
controls.classification: answer 401-402: status 200 even when a statement failed (the errors array alone reports it)

controls.name: rule-http-keeps-earlier
controls.find: if read_only && any_named(b) { store } else if any_fails(b) { store } else { store + ok_total(b) }
controls.replace: if read_only && any_named(b) { store } else { store + ok_total(b) }
controls.classification: the rule weakened (a failed request keeps its successful statements): no longer Bolt's transaction rule, so the shared-rule theorem fails

controls.name: read-only-first-only
controls.find: if read_only && any_named(b) { HOut { store: store, ran: 0, errors: 1, status: HStatus::Forbidden403 } }
controls.replace: if read_only && b.len() > 0 && b[0].names_write { HOut { store: store, ran: 0, errors: 1, status: HStatus::Forbidden403 } }
controls.classification: decision cypher_api.py 230-236 (_cypher_writes_under_read_only): only the first statement's write verdict is checked instead of any statement's; a batch whose later statement writes would run
